items.title: Ike Robertson Interview, 1961-04-28
items.q: Little Henry Rainey, that was a pretty good little trumpet player after all that opportunity with him.

ctx.x: Yes, but Chicago, he made it.
Yeah. Little Henry Rainey, that was a pretty good little trumpet player after all that opportunity with him.
He made some in the very end when his lip wasn't as good as when he was younger, I guess. Made some about 1940, I think. But if they made him ten or fifteen years before, they would have had some.

items.title: Ike Robertson Interview, 1961-04-28
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] That's right. That's right. St. Henry and Jim Robinson. [INTERVIEWEE] That's right. Some of those.

ctx.x: Actually how many years you went back footed down there by Ironton. That's why he come from a little farm that's called Ironton down the coast. It was down near the Magnolia Plantation.
That's right. That's right. St. Henry and Jim Robinson.
That's right. Some of those. Yeah. But he was just a little bit further than Magnolia. Further down the river. Yeah. He was the place where he was Ironton.
